text:
sam: Quick check-in — noticed a perf regression after yesterday's heuristic tweak when we increased max tokens-per-batch for L4 from 8k -> 12k. P95 latency on chat-gen spiked 18% for medium-length requests. Can we sync on root cause? :thinking:

maria: saw that in traces. It looks like kernel fallback is happening more often on the L4 quantized path (int4). Flame graph shows repeated small kernel invocations around the KV merge step. link: https://redwood.prod/perf/trace/1799991110 

sam: thanks. Is it KV fragmentation + larger batches causing more cache thrash?

anya: yeah, KV fragmentation is my first suspect. When batches grow, we end up with more KV pages per request and the LRU churn increases. Profiling indicates 30% higher memcpy overhead in the KV stage for those L4 runs.

ben: adding to that — kernel selector seems to prefer the fast-path kernel when seq_len <= 512, but with larger max tokens we push more requests into seq_len > 512 regions and that triggers a fallback that isn't JIT-optimized on L4. We get more small repeated kernels instead of one fused kernel.

maria: pasted the profiler snippet from the canary run:

```
# profiler summary (canary-l4-12k)
KV merge memcpy: 31.2%\nAttention kernel small-fallback: 24.8%\nDispatch overhead: 9.1%\nOther kernels: 13.7%\nIdle/wait: 21.2%\n```

ben: ugh. That matches the throughput hit. Two ways to go: 1) reduce max_tokens_per_batch for L4 temporarily, 2) change queue formation to favor padding-homogeneous batches (reduce entropy in seq_len distribution) so we stay in the fast-path kernel more often.

taylor: prototype config to rollback L4 ceiling and add padding clustering: 

```
# runtime batching config
max_tokens_per_batch: { A100: 32768, H100: 65536, A10: 16384, L4: 8192, T4: 12288 }
batch_cluster_by: ["seq_len_bucket", "model_variant"]
queue_policy: "clustered-ttl:50ms"
```

anya: cluster-by should help — it groups sequences into tighter length buckets so kernels see similar shapes. But note cluster-by increases queueing latency for some small jobs; we should set a short TTL.

sam: what's the risk if we flip L4 back to 8k tonight? Any rollback fallout?

deploy-bot: canary deployment policy: if we change max_tokens_per_batch for L4 we'll rollout to 5% of L4 fleet first and watch P95/P99, memory, and KV memcpy metrics. Auto-rollback on >10% latency regression.

maria: propose steps: 1) roll L4 ceiling back to 8k (immediate), 2) enable cluster-by with TTL 50ms on canary 5%, 3) gather 1h of traces and run differential profiler, 4) if stable at 5% for 1h, expand to 30% then 100%. I can automate the profiler job.

ben: also let's add a quick kernel-selector tweak: prefer fused kernel for seq_len in [480, 560] on L4 for 2 weeks while we test quantized-fused kernel improvements. Low-risk toggle.

anya: one more note — KV cache warmup changes with smaller batches; we should monitor cache hit ratio per-card. When we shrink L4 batches we might see hit-ratio drop initially. I'll add a metric alert if hit_ratio drops >5% within 30m.

sam: sounds good. Who will own the rollout?

taylor: I'll own the config PR and the canary rollout. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5321 (draft). I'll include the profiler dashboard and the cluster-by flag gating.

maria: I'll wire the profiler job and add a tracing dashboard panel. Also will capture sample traces for kernel selector path counts.

ben: I'll run a short microbench on A10 and T4 to ensure our cluster-by doesn't regress those card families. If anything odd appears we can make the clustering opt-in per cardclass.

sam: thanks team. Action items: taylor -> PR + canary; maria -> profiler/dashboard; ben -> microbench; anya -> KV hit alert. We'll regroup in 60m or earlier if deploy-bot flips rollback. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: canary L4 5% at 2026-03-20T22:40:00Z (manual approval pending).
